name: Sirajganj
tagline: The western gateway across the Jamuna — anchor of the great Bangabandhu Bridge, handloom heartland of Belkuchi and Shahzadpur, dairy country of Milk Vita, and the riverside estate where Tagore wrote 'Sonar Tori'.

guide.bestTime: November to February — cool, dry weather for the bridge, riverbank and terracotta temples. July to October for a full Chalan Beel and Jamuna in flood.
guide.gettingThere: By road or rail on the Dhaka–north corridor across the Bangabandhu Bridge (~3–4 hr from Dhaka). Sirajganj town and the Hard Point riverfront are on the Jamuna's west bank; Shahzadpur (Tagore's Kachharibari, Milk Vita) and the Hatikumrul temple lie ~25–40 km southwest.
guide.difficulty: Easy — the town sites and bridge zone are short road hops; Shahzadpur and Chalan Beel are day trips by bus or car. The beel needs a local boat in the wet season.

mustVisit.name: Bangabandhu (Jamuna) Bridge & Jamuna Resort
mustVisit.description: The 4.8 km bridge over the Jamuna links Sirajganj on the west bank to Tangail on the east, carrying both road and rail. The adjacent Jamuna Resort and embankment viewpoints make the west-bank approach a popular stop.
mustVisit.history: Opened to traffic in June 1998 — the 11th-longest bridge in the world at the time — it stitched the isolated northwest to Dhaka. A dedicated Jamuna Rail Bridge, inaugurated in 2025, now runs trains across alongside it.

practical.hours: Viewpoints open daylight; best at sunset

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 12–14 km north of Sirajganj town, Sadar/Kamarkhanda side (west bank)
howToReach.transport: CNG / bus to the bridge approach

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February; late afternoon for sunset
tips: Stopping on the bridge deck is restricted — use the resort and embankment viewpoints
Combine with the Bangabandhu Eco Park alongside

mustVisit.name: Rabindra Kachharibari, Shahzadpur
mustVisit.description: The Tagore family's estate revenue house in Shahzadpur, now the Rabindra Memorial Museum — holding some 331 artefacts, including a couch, chairs, piano, mirror and palanquin used by the poet himself.
mustVisit.history: Grandfather Dwarkanath Tagore bought the estate in 1840; Rabindranath first came in 1890 and returned through 1901, writing parts of Sonar Tori, Chitra and Chhinnapatra here. Around 38 of his surviving letters were written from Shahzadpur.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 40 km southwest of Sirajganj town, in Shahzadpur town

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February; Tagore festivals (Pohela Boishakh, 25 Boishakh)
tips: Carry ID for the ticket counter
Pair with Shahzadpur's Milk Vita dairy and the handloom villages nearby

mustVisit.name: Hatikumrul Navaratna Temple
mustVisit.description: A three-storied Hindu temple — the largest Navaratna (nine-spired) temple in Bangladesh, locally called the Dol Moncho — its outer walls once richly clad in terracotta plaques of deities and floral motifs.
mustVisit.history: Built around 1704–1728 by Ramnath Bhaduri, a revenue collector under Nawab Murshid Quli Khan, blending Bengali and Sikhara styles. Much of the terracotta has weathered, but the scale and form remain striking.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 25 km southwest at Hatikumrul, Ullapara Upazila, near the highway junction
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to the Hatikumrul roundabout

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February; Dol Purnima for festival colour
tips: Easy detour off the N5 / Hatikumrul roundabout
Go for the architecture and scale rather than pristine carvings

mustVisit.name: Sirajganj Hard Point & Cross Bars
mustVisit.description: A 2.5 km concrete revetment along the Jamuna's right bank, with groyne 'cross bars' jutting into the river — the town's favourite riverside promenade for strolls, picnics and sunsets.
mustVisit.history: The Hard Point was built between 1995 and 1999 to protect Sirajganj town from the Jamuna's erosion; the cross-bar groynes redirect the current and reclaim land, and have since become recreational spots.

practical.hours: Daylight; best late afternoon to sunset

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On the eastern edge of Sirajganj town, Sirajganj Sadar

tips: Cross Bar 3 ('China Bandh') is the liveliest hangout
Mind footing near the unguarded concrete edges, especially with children

mustVisit.name: Bangabandhu Eco Park
mustVisit.description: An eco park laid out near the west-bank approach of the Bangabandhu Bridge — greenery, walking trails and river views, a family picnic complement to the bridge and resort.
mustVisit.history: Developed alongside the bridge tourism zone after the 1998 opening, as part of the Jamuna Resort eco-tourism cluster.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 13 km north of town beside the bridge approach, Sadar/Kamarkhanda
howToReach.transport: CNG / bus to the bridge zone

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February; mornings for birds
tips: Loop it with the bridge viewpoint and Jamuna Resort
Carry water and snacks — on-site food is limited

mustVisit.name: Chalan Beel (Tarash)
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's largest inland wetland, shared across Sirajganj, Natore and Pabna — a vast monsoon expanse of water, fish and birds that shrinks to farmland in the dry season. The Sirajganj share lies mainly in Tarash.
mustVisit.history: About a tenth of Chalan Beel falls in Tarash upazila. The beel is a relic of an old river floodplain and a historic fishing and rice bowl of the region.

practical.hours: Daylight; boating in the wet season

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 45–55 km west/southwest, Tarash (and Ullapara) Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Tarash, then local boat

mustVisit.bestTime: July to October for full water; winter for migratory birds
tips: Hire a local boat from a Tarash landing for the full beel
Go with a local guide — access points shift with the season

specialties.name: Tant Handloom Saris
specialties.description: Sirajganj is one of Bangladesh's largest handloom hubs, weaving saris, lungis, bedsheets and three-pieces. The looms cluster in Belkuchi, Shahzadpur, Enayetpur and Ullapara, with the Shohagpur cloth market at their heart.

specialties.name: Enayetpur Pantua
specialties.description: Sirajganj's signature sweet — a fried chhana dumpling in syrup, credited to the confectioner Ganesh Modak of Enayetpur about a century ago.

specialties.name: Milk Vita Dairy (Baghabari)
specialties.description: Bangladesh's pioneering dairy cooperative set up its first pasteurization plant at Baghabari, Shahzadpur, in 1973 — and the district remains a national milk heartland, rich in ghee and chhana sweets.

bucketlist.title: Watch sunset over the Bangabandhu Bridge
bucketlist.detail: The 4.8 km bridge that stitched the northwest to Dhaka in 1998 — best from the west-bank resort and embankment as the Jamuna turns gold.

bucketlist.title: Stand in Tagore's Shahzadpur Kachharibari
bucketlist.detail: The estate house where Rabindranath wrote parts of Sonar Tori between 1890 and 1901 — now a museum of 331 artefacts, including his piano and palanquin.

bucketlist.title: Circle the nine spires of Hatikumrul
bucketlist.detail: The largest Navaratna temple in Bangladesh — a three-storey terracotta shrine built by Ramnath Bhaduri around 1704–1728.

bucketlist.title: Stroll the Hard Point at golden hour
bucketlist.detail: A 2.5 km riverside promenade on the Jamuna where the town walks, picnics and watches the sun drop behind the chars.

bucketlist.title: Watch a tant loom at work in Belkuchi
bucketlist.detail: One of the country's biggest handloom belts — the clack of shuttles weaving saris, lungis and bedsheets across Belkuchi and Enayetpur.

bucketlist.title: Eat pantua at its Enayetpur birthplace
bucketlist.detail: A fried chhana sweet in syrup, made by the descendants of Ganesh Modak who created it here about a century ago.

bucketlist.title: Drink fresh milk in Milk Vita country
bucketlist.detail: Baghabari in Shahzadpur built Bangladesh's first dairy pasteurization plant in 1973 — this is the nation's milk heartland.

bucketlist.title: Boat across Chalan Beel in flood
bucketlist.detail: Bangladesh's largest inland wetland, brimming in monsoon with water, fish and birds — the Sirajganj share is in Tarash.

bucketlist.title: Picnic at Bangabandhu Eco Park
bucketlist.detail: Green walking trails and river views beside the bridge approach — the family complement to the Jamuna viewpoints.

bucketlist.title: Cross on the new Jamuna Rail Bridge
bucketlist.detail: Inaugurated in 2025, the dedicated rail bridge runs trains across the Jamuna at speed alongside the road bridge.

bucketlist.title: Buy Shahzadpur ghee and chhana sweets
bucketlist.detail: The dairy economy that feeds Milk Vita also turns out fine ghee and chhana-based mishti around Shahzadpur.

bucketlist.title: Hang out at Cross Bar 3 ('China Bandh')
bucketlist.detail: The most popular of the groyne cross bars jutting into the Jamuna — the town's go-to evening spot.

foods.name: Enayetpur Pantua
foods.description: Sirajganj's signature sweet — a fried chhana dumpling soaked in syrup, credited to Ganesh Modak of Enayetpur about a century ago.

foods.name: Shahzadpur Ghee & Chhana Sweets
foods.description: As a dairy heartland, the Shahzadpur–Baghabari belt is known for rich ghee and milk-based mishti.

foods.name: Milk Vita Dairy
foods.description: Fresh milk, butter and ghee from Bangladesh's pioneering dairy cooperative, whose first plant rose at Baghabari in 1973.

famousPeople.name: Syed Ismail Hossain Siraji
famousPeople.knownFor: Poet, writer and reformer of the Bengali Muslim reawakening, born in Sirajganj in 1880. His first poetry book, Anal-Prabaha, was banned by the British government and he was imprisoned — often called the first South Asian poet jailed for calling for independence.

famousPeople.name: Mahadev Saha
famousPeople.knownFor: One of modern Bengali poetry's most-loved romantic and protest voices, author of dozens of collections. Born 5 August 1944 at Dhanghara in Sirajganj; awarded the Ekushey Padak (2001) and the Independence Award (2021).

famousPeople.name: Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani
famousPeople.knownFor: Towering social reformer and peasant-rights leader known as the 'Majlum Jananeta' (leader of the oppressed). Born around 1880 at Dhangara village in the Sirajganj region, he spent his life organising the rural poor across Bengal and Assam.

didYouKnow: The Bangabandhu (Jamuna) Bridge, opened in June 1998 at 4.8 km, was the 11th-longest bridge in the world at the time — and made Sirajganj the western gateway between Dhaka and the north.
Sirajganj is one of Bangladesh's largest handloom (tant) weaving hubs; Belkuchi, Shahzadpur and Enayetpur clothe much of the country in saris, lungis and bedsheets.
Milk Vita, the country's flagship dairy cooperative, built its first pasteurization plant at Baghabari in Shahzadpur in 1973 — Sirajganj is a national dairy heartland.
Rabindranath Tagore wrote parts of Sonar Tori and Chhinnapatra at the Shahzadpur Kachharibari, which still holds some 331 of the poet's artefacts.
The Hatikumrul Navaratna Temple (c. 1704–1728) is the largest nine-spired temple in Bangladesh.
About a tenth of Chalan Beel, Bangladesh's largest inland wetland, lies within Sirajganj's Tarash upazila.
